subject.title: Node host: no SSH transport support + challenge auth fails behind reverse proxy

question: Should `openclaw node run` gain first-class managed SSH transport using `gateway.remote.*`, or should node-host SSH remain a documented external tunnel while direct `wss://` pairing/auth is handled in the remote-node approval track?
rationale: This changes remote node-host transport supervision and pairing locality/security semantics, so automation should not choose the trust boundary or product shape.

options.title: Define managed node-host SSH
options.body: Specify SSH lifecycle, credential precedence, and pairing semantics, then implement the narrow core path with live tunnel and reverse-proxy proof.

options.title: Split auth from transport
options.body: Keep this issue focused on managed SSH transport and route the direct `wss://` node approval behavior to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/91126.

options.title: Document manual tunnels only
options.body: Decide not to manage node-host SSH in core and update docs/diagnostics while keeping remote-node auth work separate.

recommendation.title: Define managed node-host SSH
recommendation.body: Specify SSH lifecycle, credential precedence, and pairing semantics, then implement the narrow core path with live tunnel and reverse-proxy proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant node-host, SSH, and pairing/security history is strongest under this account.
